The six reconcile jobs are external technical reconciliation - they verify the leads against primary sources and correct the inherited prose - and they supply the evidence the compare jobs then state against the Plans. That is the designed division of labour, and it means this arm's recall is a function of how many leads reached COMPARE, not how many reached reconcile.

comparison_with_claude_hicap.verdict: PRIORITIZATION LOST. Arm P scored 32 against claude-hicap's 45 on identical inputs - a net loss of 13 findings - despite comparing 16 leads to claude-hicap's 14 and spending $85.50 against claude-hicap's $82.52.
comparison_with_claude_hicap.why: The 19 findings lost are not scattered: they are two coherent families the ranking pushed below rank 16. The external-editor and diff family - F029, F031, F032, F034, F036, F037, F053, F028, F087 - and the graph and history family - F062, F066, F088, F092, F107, F043, F059, F074, F083, F106. Muse Spark's top 16 are almost entirely backup closure, GC fencing, store integrity, colocation certification and identity. Its own stated reasons show why: nine of the top ten name operation recovery, GC, closure, colocation or config. The prioritizer optimised for one theme and got depth in it.
comparison_with_claude_hicap.what_prioritization_did_buy: The 6 gained findings are real and they are where the extra depth went: F005 and F019 come from reading the concurrency and stale-workspace material to the bottom, F052 and F057 from checking two defects against the exact v0.44.0 tag rather than by release dating, and F054 and F064 are reached by NO continuation-4 arm at all.

ranking_yield.question: Which ranks produced credits?
ranking_yield.reading: THE YIELD IS FLAT, AND THAT IS THE RESULT. Ranks 11-13 produced 7 credits, exactly as many as ranks 1-3; ranks 14-16 produced 5, as many as ranks 8-10. The prioritizer's ordering did not predict yield. If the ranking had been informative, credits would decline with rank; they do not. Rank 7 produced the fewest (2) only because it was a single-lead job.
ranking_yield.consequence: Because yield per lead is roughly constant across the compared band, the arm's recall is governed by HOW MANY leads reached compare and WHICH FAMILIES they belong to - not by their order. Arm P compared two more leads than claude-hicap and still lost 13 findings, because the 16 it compared were thematically concentrated while claude-hicap's 14, taken in frozen order, spanned more families.
ranking_yield.caveat: This measures yield against the 110-finding union only. The ranking may well have optimised for something else - the top-ranked leads did produce this arm's deepest contract repairs, and two findings no other arm reached.

coverage_vs_other_arms.note: premium union hybrid is the whole 110-finding union by construction, so nothing can fall outside it; the substantive statement is that this arm delivered no proposition I could credit as a finding the union does not already contain.

reached_delivery_fraction.reading: Everything admitted got there, at both stages, including the session-limited job. There is no 'did not get there' loss inside the admitted set. The arm's misses are entirely a function of which 16 of 88 leads were admitted.

cost.comparability: Comparable with claude-hicap ($82.5164, 45 credits, $1.834 per finding) because the per-job limits are identical. Arm P cost $2.672 per credited finding - 46% more per finding. NOT comparable with the goal-2 arms or the 40-response continuation-4 arms.
cost.prioritization_was_nearly_free: The ranking pass cost $0.011961 - 0.014% of the arm's spend. Whatever else is true, prioritization is cheap; it is the admission budget it steers that is expensive.

timing.vs_claude_hicap: claude-hicap arm wall 3,535.2 s; Arm P 4,193.3 s. Arm P is 18.6% slower for 13 fewer findings.

limits: One frozen case, one ordering, one prioritizer. This does not establish that prioritization cannot help - only that THIS ranking, on THIS union, lost.

Two variables moved at once: admission order AND effort (max vs claude-hicap's xhigh). The ordering effect is not cleanly isolated, and the effort difference runs in Arm P's favour, which makes the 13-finding loss a conservative estimate of the ordering penalty.

Recall is measured against continuation 3's fixed 110-finding union, which was built from premium and hybrid output. A prioritizer that optimises for anything the union does not contain is penalised here by construction - see ranking_yield.caveat.

The 110-finding union is not a yield oracle. 'Lost' findings are findings claude-hicap reached and this arm did not; they are not necessarily more valuable than the deeper contract repairs Arm P produced in its own band.
'Unsupported or already-covered' is a union class, not a false-positive rate.
Adjudicator and the depth-stage model share a family; all 23 code facts were independently verified against pinned bytes to make the judgement re-checkable.
